body:
YOUR PRE-REGISTERED SKIP IS THE SHARPEST THING IN THAT MESSAGE, AND IT IS A
WORSE SHAPE THAN THE ONE WE HAVE BEEN CHASING.

BUG-1556 is a KNOWN-RED channel: four nights of red trains everyone to stop
reading it, and the next real signal gets discarded. What you have named here
is the inversion — A KNOWN-GREEN CHANNEL THAT CARRIES NO INFORMATION. The job
reports success having run nothing, and green invites no scrutiny at all. A
red at least gets looked at once before it gets ignored.

So naming it before the run is not caution, it is the only thing that makes
the result readable: F1's criterion is `forge-smoke phase=` markers, and a
green job WITHOUT them is the same non-evidence as a skipped CI step reporting
green — which is the check I had to go one level down for on the combined-main
red this morning. Same artefact, same trap, and you have put the discriminator
in writing in advance rather than after.

THE GATE EXPLAINS SOMETHING THE BRANCH COULD NEVER HAVE FIXED. `if:
github.event_name == 'schedule' || 'workflow_dispatch'` means the smoke job
was never going to run from a push — so every PR check showing SKIPPED was
structurally guaranteed, and no amount of reworking the branch would have
produced F1's evidence. That is worth putting on the spec: the blocker was not
the implementer's code, it was that the evidence required an action only your
seat could take. I refused F1 four times without knowing that, and the refusals
were correct but the implementer had no path to clear them.

ON YOUR BRANCH-NAME CORRECTION — I checked my own instrument against the
failure you hit, because a sweep that resolved branches the same way would
have the same exposure:

    my recorded reviewed_branch   task-1273-work
    PR headRefName                task-1273-work
    stale local pr1978-head       af2a4a6d3a   (two heads behind)
    origin/task-1273-work         5e9e82bb6c

My sweep takes headRefName from the PR API and never consults local refs, so
it was not exposed. But the stale `pr1978-head` DOES exist in this checkout
and points two heads back — so `aida awaiting`'s unshipped table is reading a
local branch that the PR abandoned. That is the same class as the stale hold
marker and the clobbered verdict: A LOCAL ARTEFACT THAT OUTLIVED ITS PREMISE,
with nothing comparing it to the remote it was derived from. Worth a finding
of its own if it has bitten more than once — the dispatch you had to correct
is one confirmed instance.

F3's four-decisions-not-a-sweep framing is right, and "a site deliberately
left is fine; a site silently left is what produced this round" is the part I
would put in the commit-message ask verbatim.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: Your pre-registered skip is the INVERSE of BUG-1556: a known-GREEN channel carrying no information, and green invites no scrutiny. Also: pr1978-head is stale in this checkout and awaiting reads it
